thread:
zoe: Heads-up from the quarterly least-priv sweep: found multiple orphaned principals and two service accounts with cross-account KMS grants in prod. None have a current owner in our inventory.

li: can you share the export? need last_used and roles.

zoe: uploaded csv -> https://drive.internal/redwood/access-reviews/4108889990_orphans.csv. columns: principal, env, last_used_ts, roles, kms_grants

michael: if they have kms grants we must not blind-delete. propose: 1) create SecTracker tickets with evidence, 2) 72hr claim window, 3) dry-run removal in staging, 4) if KMS-bound, run key rotation handshake before revoke.

sam: +1. also add `requires-sec-eng-approval` label for any external principals. I'll script a dry-run that prints impacted keys and callers.

security-bot: [policy] Ownerless principals with persistent KMS grants require two-person approval before emergency revoke. Flagged items: 9 total, 3 with kms grants.

zoe: timeline: start triage today. sam please run dry-run and post findings. michael and I will craft the ticket template: claimed_by, evidence_link, risk_level, kms_handshake_required.

michael: For KMS-bound items: plan to provision a temporary key, update callers in a canary cohort, monitor decrypt failures for 30m, then rotate callers and revoke original grants. add monitor threshold: 4 failed decrypts / 5m -> page eng-oncall.

oncall-bot: monitor created "kms-handshake-4108889990" -> pages eng-oncall on breach.

li: I'll compile PR history to show recent usage as evidence for each ticket. If no evidence, mark high risk and schedule revoke after SLA.

zoe: good. final note: attach audit snapshot (IAM bindings + last-used logs) to each SecTracker ticket for the audit team. I'll update the thread when tickets are created. :white_check_mark:
